newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arab anger and frustration cloud West Bank.
newsitem.headline: Arab anger and frustration cloud West Bank.

text.p: Frustration and anger swept through a West Bank village on Wednesday where hundreds of Arab students paid condolences to the family of a Palestinian policeman killed by Israeli soldiers.
The visitors mourned not only the officer, Haitham Mansour, who died at the age of 20 on Tuesday, but also peace.
"How can there be peace when they are still shooting to kill," said a 23-year-old student who gave her name only as Sana. "I am worried about the future."
Women in black clothes sent shudders through the crowd when they ululated for Mansour.
The undercover policeman was near a crowd demonstrating on the outskirts of the Palestinian town of Nablus when Israeli soldiers opened fire, hitting him in the head and killing him instantly.

Such stone-throwing protests, met by Israeli rubber bullets and occasionally live ammunition, have become a daily ritual in the West Bank since Israel sent bulldozers to break ground for a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem two weeks ago.
Mansour was the third Palestinian killed by Israeli gunfire in the current wave of violence.
"Haitham is not only our martyr and son. He is your martyr, brother and son as well," Mansour's 75-year-old grandfather Abdel-Latif Salem told the students.
"Unfortunately, no one learns a lesson after the victims fall," he said.
The violence has plunged Palestinians deeper into despair. Israeli put its troops in the West Bank on alert and deployed tanks and armoured vehicles on the outskirts of some Palestinian towns.

Israeli tanks put on a show of force near Nablus on Wednesday as the students embarked on their mission to offer condolences to Mansour's family in Kufr Qallil, tucked on a hillside on the edge of the town.
The students watched the tanks from the village.
"The Israelis say that we practice violence. But violence is also coming from their side. I think we ought to stop this violence once and for all," Sana said.
In the West Bank town of Hebron, where Palestinian buried another youth shot dead by Israeli soldiers on Tuesday, the mood was no less grim.
"I do not see a quick end to the violence. I see a catastrophe on the way," said Zalikha al-Muhtaseb, a school teacher.

"They are demanding that the Palestinian Authority stop terror, but it is their terror that ought to be stopped. How can they expect calm when they are confiscating our lands, building settlements and killing our dream of independence?" she said.
